owner_decision_unchanged: 48/48/64 stays frozen. The standardization decision rests on C1/C2/C3, which hold.
the_criterion_is_the_defect: C4 was predeclared as a WALL-CLOCK bound on a shared laptop. Wall clock is a property of the machine, not of the algorithm, so C4 measures load. The repo's own standing lesson says exactly this -- report a load-independent work counter, never seconds alone -- and I did not follow it when I sealed the criteria. That is a defect in MY criterion, not a finding about the route widths.
what_happened: An independent re-run of the SAME deterministic check, on the same code and the same pinned kernel, reproduced the chemistry exactly and FLIPPED the verdict GREEN -> NOT_GREEN on the cost criterion alone.
what_is_NOT_being_done: The criteria are NOT relaxed and the check is NOT being re-run on a quiet machine until it passes. Re-running to get the other answer is measuring until the answer changes. Both runs are committed side by side.
what_the_safety_decision_actually_rests_: C1, C2 and C3 -- recovery, yield and exact containment -- are load-independent and reproduced EXACTLY across both runs: identical eligible sets, 0 lost, 0 gained, 10 eligible per arm. Those are the criteria that decide whether standardizing to 48/48/64 is SAFE, and they are unaffected.
